Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: Comprehensive district-wide inventory including building sizes, ages, portables, and detailed site plans; robust condition assessments covering HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical, lighting, technology infrastructure, and accessibility; integrates condition data with student outcomes and long-term capital planning (e.g., Sections 2.0, 5.2, site assessments, and project descriptions).

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: Detailed enrollment projections with methodology explained; capacity utilization data by site and classroom; explicit connection of enrollment trends to facility actions including new construction, consolidation, and adaptive uses; includes innovative space uses like wellness hubs and community partnerships (Sections 1.4, 3.0, and site-specific capacity analyses).

Educational Alignment.justification: Educational alignment is a core organizing principle with detailed educational specifications for all school levels; clear integration of district mission, instructional priorities, and facilities planning; facility projects directly respond to educational needs including STEM labs, makerspaces, special education, and technology-rich environments (Section 5.1 Educational Specifications and throughout site project descriptions).

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: District-wide data on outdoor spaces including turf, hardcourts, playgrounds, and shade structures; detailed strategies for campus greening such as expanded tree cover, permeable surfaces, outdoor classrooms, rain gardens, and stormwater management; outdoor learning and environmental literacy are integrated into planning (site plans and project lists for all campuses, e.g., Alvarado ES, Hillview Crest ES).

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: Plan acknowledges climate-related risks such as drainage and heat with some mitigation strategies like shade structures and improved drainage; however, lacks comprehensive district-wide climate risk assessment or multi-hazard analysis; climate readiness is a consideration but not a central theme (references to drainage improvements, shade structures, and solar panels but no detailed climate risk assessment).

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: Includes energy efficiency strategies such as solar photovoltaic systems, HVAC upgrades, and LED lighting; references energy resilience goals and some renewable integration; mentions compliance with Title 24 and state goals but lacks comprehensive district-wide energy data and detailed electrification or microgrid plans (site project descriptions and completed projects include solar and HVAC upgrades).

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: Presents a comprehensive capital strategy with detailed cost estimates, escalation assumptions, and soft cost calculations; clear prioritization framework across safety, equity, modernization, and climate resilience; multiple funding strategies including local bonds, state grants, and developer fees; considers long-term financial sustainability and aligns with educational priorities (Section 5.2 Cost Assessment and Escalation Summaries and project cost breakdowns).
